before_conditions: The DistributionCreator contract accepts arbitrary ERC20 tokens for reward distribution.
The internal accounting logic in increaseTokenBalance assumes that the balance increase in the contract exactly matches the input amount parameter.
The increaseTokenBalance function updates the user's internal ledger (creatorBalance) using the input amount parameter, ignoring the actual number of tokens received by the contract.
A user deposits a Fee-on-Transfer token (or a token with transfer inaccuracies such as stETH) into the contract.
The contract receives fewer tokens than the input amount due to the token's transfer fee or rounding loss.
The user's creatorBalance is credited with the full input amount, which is greater than the actual tokens received by the contract.
required_property: The contract's internal accounting (sum of all creatorBalance ledgers) should always be backed by at least an equivalent amount of physically held tokens, ensuring that any user can later withdraw or use their full recorded balance without failure, regardless of the token type deposited.
bad_outcome: The contract becomes insolvent because its physical token balance is less than the sum of all creatorBalance ledgers. When a user attempts to use their recorded balance, the transaction reverts due to insufficient contract balance, resulting in a permanent denial of service and fund loss for the last user attempting to withdraw or use their balance.
